reference.description: What the conversation is about: 'Romans 8:28' or 'Romans 8'; in a talk from a screen (`screen` is present), the screen's name.

greek.description: The Greek of the verse or of the passage under a heading (the whole passage), or of the chapter's first three verses. Missing in a talk from a screen (`screen` is present), which is not about a text.

english.description: The same text in English (the Majority Standard Bible), of the same verses. Words the translators supplied are between asterisks (*was* king): they are in italics in his reader. Missing in a talk from a screen.

greek_words.description: Optional. The words of `greek`, in text order, each with its form as it stands in the text, its lemma (the dictionary form), the lexicon's gloss and its parsing in plain words, from the app's own chapter data; a word the text repeats with the same lemma and parsing is listed once. For a long passage the list may stop part-way. Missing in a talk from a screen.

spoken.description: Optional. true only when he spoke the question to the phone's English speech recogniser (Hold to talk, Hold to ask); missing when he typed it. A Greek word in it may have come as English sound-alikes. See the instructions.

history.description: The last turns of the conversation, oldest first.

mode.description: Optional. quiz: the reader chose Quiz me on the verse or passage `reference` names; the grind runs the quizzing and mapping method on `greek` and `english`.

study_way.description: Optional, and only in a quiz (mode quiz). The reader's own lines about how he wants the read, quiz and map method run (My study way in the app), oldest first, at most 12, each at most 100 characters; he kept each one himself. Where a line conflicts with the default method, the line wins. Missing when he has kept none.

quiz_goal.description: Optional, and only in a quiz (mode quiz). Why the reader wants the quiz, in his words (Quiz goal in the app, at most 80 characters), or null when he has kept none: the quiz then opens by asking him why.

quiz_goal_once.description: Optional, and only in a quiz with `quiz_goal` null. A goal he chose 'Just this time' for earlier in this quiz (at most 80 characters): quiz to match it, do not ask again and do not offer to keep it again.

pending_offer.description: Optional. Present only while an offer of yours waits for his tap: the newest such offer of this conversation. `kind` is 'feedback' (Send this to the makers; `text` is the summary it would send), 'setting' (a setting change from `setting_offer`; `text` is what it would change, such as 'Change Theme: Dark') 'quiz-goal' (the goal from `quiz_goal_offer`; `text` is the goal), 'bridge' (your `bridge`; `text` is 'Take me there: <title of the idea it opens>'; his yes opens that idea's sheet) 'greek' (your `greek_offer`; `text` is its line; his yes opens the Greek word or switches the Reader to Greek, and his no is kept by the app in the memory index) or 'rusty' (your `rusty_offer`; `text` is 'Move back to Frontier and practise'; his yes moves the rusty items you named back to Frontier and opens their practice). Decide from `question` whether he confirms, declines or asks to hear it, and say so in `offer_reply`.

reader_view.description: Optional. Which language the Reader shows him now: 'english' or 'greek' (what he chose with English | Greek at the top of the Reader). Missing in a talk from a screen. Only a reader whose Reader is 'english' and who is not otherwise learning the Greek is offered the Greek (`greek_offer`); see the instructions, 'Offering the Greek'.

missing_foundations.description: Optional. Present only when the grammar words of his question name a topic that rests on ideas he has not learned (not yet, or not at all): `topic` is the idea he asked about, `total` how many ideas under it he lacks, and `ideas` the lowest on the ladder first (at most 8), so `ideas[0]` is his next step in the progression. `direct` marks an idea the topic itself names as a need: those are the most important. Offer a `bridge` from this list and never name an idea that is not in it (see the instructions, 'When he is not ready for the question').

topic.description: The title of the idea he asked about: 'The genitive case'.

total.description: How many ideas under the topic he lacks, all of them (the list names at most 8).

id.description: The idea's id, to put in `bridge`.

title.description: The idea's title, as he sees it: 'Pairs of vowels'.

direct.description: true when the topic itself names this idea as a need.

resources.description: Optional. The study resources he has switched on in Settings, in the order Settings lists them: the only ones the answer's `links` may count on. An empty list means none is on. Missing only in a talk from About.

id.description: The resource's key: strongs, logos or accordance.

name.description: What Settings calls it: Strong's, Logos, Accordance.

words.description: True when a word's entry can be opened in it (a link of kind word).

verses.description: True when a verse can be opened in it (a link of kind verse).

screen.description: Optional. Present when he asked from a full screen of the app (the round Ask the tutor button) and not about a text: the screen's name (Goal, Words, Review, Quick test, Parsing drill, Paradigms, Placement, Settings, My study way, Import, About) and what the screen shows, as labelled facts (on Goal: the goal, the solid, frontier and not yet counts of its words and grammar ideas, Learn next and the Next words). `greek` and `english` are then missing.

settings.description: Only on Settings: every setting and study-resource switch the screen has, each with the value it holds now (On, Off, Dark, 0.8x) and the line shown under it. A setting that is Off is listed too.

credits.description: Only on About: every source Lampas credits, each with its name, what it gives this reader, its licence (or why none is needed) and its link.

form.description: Optional. Present while he is being helped to fill in a form of the app (the button 'Let the tutor help me fill this in'): the form's name and its fields in screen order, each with the name you answer with, the label he sees, the hint under it if any, whether it is required, its kind and what it holds now ('' when empty; for pictures, how many he has added). `screen` is also present, with the form's name and no facts; `greek` and `english` are missing.

name.description: The field's key: the name `form_values` and `form_ask` use.

label.description: What the form calls the field on screen.

hint.description: The line under the field, when the form has one.

required.description: Whether the form cannot be sent without it.

kind.description: text: any words; link: a web address; pictures: screenshots or photos, which only he can add (you cannot fill them).

value.description: What the field holds now, cut at 600 characters; empty when nothing is in it. For pictures, a count such as '2 pictures added'.

solid_words.description: The Greek lemmas he already knows well.

learner.description: Optional. Where he stands in one line: 'solid N words; learning: a, b, c; new today: x, y; due now: M'.

learner_grammar.description: Optional (an older app does not send it). Where his grammar stands: the reading goal, how many of its words and grammar ideas are solid, at the frontier and not yet, the titles of the ideas at each level (the goal's needs first, at most 12 a list), whether he has been placed, the move the app's New words at setting should make, the grammar approach with its next lesson, and his weak points from Drill it. At most 900 bytes.

goal.description: His reading goal, 'Read 1 John 1:1', or null.

words.description: How many of the goal's words (with no goal, of his own words) are solid, being learned (frontier) and not yet.

ideas.description: The titles of the grammar ideas at each level, the goal's needs first, then by rung; at most 12 a list.

placed.description: Whether he has taken the grammar placement.

suggested_move.description: up: his grammar reviews go well, New words at could move to frontier grammar; down: they go badly, it could move to solid grammar; none.

picker_level.description: What the setting New words at holds now.

name.description: The grammar approach he follows: 'BMA Tutor'.

credit.description: Whom the approach is credited to, or null.

next_lesson.description: The title of the lesson he would learn next, or null when he has met every idea.

weak.description: Optional (missing when there are none). His weak points from Drill it, the app's practice on one grammar idea at a time: the title of an idea he drilled (the one drilled longest ago first) to the short labels of the things in it he missed and has not yet got, such as 'its ending' or 'ν (Nu)'. The latest drill of an idea decides: once a later drill proves the idea, it is not listed. At most 5 ideas, 3 labels each.

memory.description: Optional. What Lampas remembers about him, which the app keeps on his phone (Settings > Memory) and chose for this ask: `index` is the short index of everything remembered (his own lines, then a list of the notes, one line each: the note's name and its first line), and `notes` are the notes the app picked by name for this place, word or screen (`book:<Book>` for the book of the reference, `word:<lemma>` for the word he asked about, `topic:<screen>` for the screen he is on), each `name` and `text`. At most three; read the index first, then the notes. Use it quietly as `learner_profile` is used: let it shape the answer, never repeat it back to him, and never let it change what is true about the text. Missing when nothing is kept.

index.description: The index as it is kept, at most 1500 characters; may be empty when only notes are named.

learner_profile.description: Optional. Who he is as a student, which he kept himself in Settings > About you; every field is optional and a field he has not filled in is missing (the whole field is missing when he has filled in none). age: a number or a band, as he wrote it. pace: how fast he wants to go. ways: how he learns best (hearing, seeing, reading, doing = hands-on). background: languages he knows, Greek or Bible before, in his words. why: why he is learning Greek, in his words. notes: short things the tutor has learned about him, the newest last. Meet him where he is; never repeat this back to him. learned, observed_pace, observed_ways and do_not_ask are what the app itself found out; see them as hints at the same fields, weaker than what he wrote.

learned.description: What the tutor itself learned about him in earlier talks, for a field he did not fill in himself: field, value, and guessed true when it is only a guess from how he writes and talks (never state a guess as a fact, and let anything he told you or chose win over it).

observed_pace.description: How he seems to go, which the phone worked out from how fast and how rightly he answers in reviews, quizzes and drills: quick, steady or slow. Missing until he has answered enough. It may differ from the `pace` he chose; his choice wins.

observed_ways.description: What he uses, as whole percents the phone counted: hearing (verses and words said aloud), seeing (pictures he sent), reading (chapters and verses read) and doing (quiz, review and drill answers, readings aloud). A way with no use is left out; missing until he has used the app enough. A hint at how he likes to learn, not a fact.

do_not_ask.description: The profile fields you must not ask him about in this talk: asked in the last day, or he declined to say. Missing when none.

rusty.description: Optional. The solid words and grammar ideas he now slips on (a wrong answer among his last three) or has not met for a long while (a week or more past due), worst first, at most 8. Each: `kind` 'word' or 'idea', `id` (the word's dictionary form, or the idea's id), `title` (what to call it) and `why` (the plain reason, such as 'slipped twice this week' or 'not seen for 3 weeks'). Missing when nothing is rusty, and in a quiz. It is the app's own list, worked out from his answers: never add an item to it or name one that is not in it (see the instructions, 'When he has gone rusty').

requests.description: Optional. The requests he has sent to the factory (an ask the tutor offered to pass on, an approach he asked for), at most the 10 newest, newest first, each with where it stands. Missing when he has sent none. status: sent (the factory has it, nothing more yet), filed (the makers have it on their list), building (being built now), landed (built and shipped; `version` is the app version it is in), declined (the makers decided not to; `reason` is why) or adopted-as-setting (it became a setting; `setting` is where Settings has it). Answer 'what happened to my idea' from this, never from a guess.

summary.description: What he asked for, in one line.

version.description: Only with landed: the app version the idea shipped in.

setting.description: Only with adopted-as-setting: the setting's name, as the makers wrote it ('Settings > Appearance > Sepia').

reason.description: Only with declined: why, in one plain sentence.

pictures.description: Optional. How many pictures he sent with this message (1 to 4): they are attached to the request as image files, in the order he added them, and belong to this message only. Missing when he sent none. The `question` may then be only 'Read the picture and tell me about it.'

settings.description: What each of the app's settings holds now, by key.

pronunciation.description: Optional. The Greek pronunciation the app speaks and respells in, by its id: modern (how Greek is spoken today). Describe every Greek sound by it.

focus.description: Optional. What he asked for help with: a word (from the word sheet's Help with this word row, or its Ask the tutor: the form as it stands, its lemma, its parsing in plain words, and what he wants help with), a grammar term (from a Grammar sheet's Ask the tutor), a paradigm table (from the Paradigms screen's Ask the tutor), or a Quick test question (from the question's Ask the tutor: the word, the question, his answer and his earlier answers of the round).

kind.description: grammar: the form and what is needed to read it; sound: its syllables and how each sounds; word: just the word, with nothing in particular asked.

language.description: Only for a Hebrew word of an answer (the Hebrew guide's Syllables and sounds): he. Absent for a Greek word.

respelling.description: Only for a Greek word's sound question: the word as the app's pronunciation respells it, the stressed syllable in capitals (ταῦτα is TAF-ta). Describe each syllable's sound by it.

syllables.description: Only for a Greek word's sound question: the word cut into syllables by the app, in order, in Greek letters. Use these exactly; never count or cut the word yourself.

stress.description: Only with syllables: the 0-based index of the stressed syllable in syllables (0 is the first). Absent when the word carries no accent.

term.description: The grammar term he asked about, as the word sheet's Parsing writes it: conjunction, aorist, genitive, 3rd person ...

kind.description: grammar-term: explain this term in plain words.

table.description: The paradigm table he is learning, by its name on the Paradigms screen: The article, Noun endings, εἰμί, Verb endings.

revealed.description: The forms of the table he has revealed, each with its place: 'Genitive Singular Masculine: τοῦ'. May be empty.

kind.description: paradigm: explain the table's pattern and quiz him on the forms he has revealed.
quiz: he answered a Quick test question and asks about the word.

lemma.description: The word's dictionary form, the one the question asked.

form.description: The form the word has in the chapter he is reading, when it has one there.

parse.description: That form's parsing in plain words, when the chapter has the form.

pos.description: The word's part of speech: noun, verb ...

question.description: The question as he saw it: What does νόμος mean?

right.description: Whether what he chose was the right gloss.

answers.description: His answers to the earlier questions of this round, oldest first. May be empty.
